title: Edge Telemetry Validation and Onboarding Playbook for Enterprise Tenants
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the recommended validation, onboarding workflow, and operational handoff for enterprise customers connecting edge or client-side telemetry (web SDKs, mobile SDKs, edge ingestion proxies) into Redwood’s telemetry pipeline. It focuses on minimizing false positives in alerts, ensuring SLO alignment, and providing clear escalation and rollback steps for integration engineers and customer success teams.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise tenants connecting production telemetry for: request traces, sampling events, client-side metrics (latency, token counts), and structured request metadata (tenant_id, route, model_version).
- Covers both SaaS-hosted customers and Dedicated/Private tenants where telemetry is proxied through a sidecar.
- Excludes proprietary third-party observability adapters (see related pages for adapter guides).

Owner and contact information:
- Playbook owner: Maya Chen (Customer Reliability Lead) — maya@redwood.com
- Primary oncall for telemetry ingestion: telemetry-oncall@redwood.com
- Engineering consult: eng-observability@redwood.com
- Customer Success (CS) handoff alias: cs-ops@redwood.com

Goals and acceptance criteria (must be green before handback):
1) Events accepted and parsed without >1% schema failures over 10,000 test events.
2) Ingress latency for validated events <200ms p95 to telemetry-gatekeeper in the customer region.
3) No more than 0.05% increase in global alert noise attributable to new tenant in the first 72 hours.
4) SLOs for tenant-specific dashboards created and reviewed with customer stakeholders.

Key services and components (names used in commands below):
- ingress-gateway (edge ingress HTTP/2 endpoints)
- telemetry-gatekeeper (validation and rate-limiting service)
- tenant-metrics-proxy (tenant-aware proxy that scrubs PII)
- observability-collector (aggregator -> timeseries/long-term storage)

Prerequisites from customer before starting:
- A test API key generated with telemetry:write scope and tenant_id provided.
- Network allowlist for Redwood ingress IPs (list provided by CS).
- A short test dataset (500–2,000 synthetic events) mapped to expected client SDK shapes.
- Designated technical contact and test window (2 hours).

Validation checklist (pre-cutover):
- 1) Schema validation tests
  - Use the test harness to run the sample suite against telemetry-gatekeeper. Expected result: schema_failures = 0 (or <= 1% of events).
  - Example curl payload (JSON):
    curl -X POST https://ingress-gateway.redwood.example/v1/events \n      -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \n      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n      -d '{"tenant_id":"acme-corp","event_type":"generation_request","timestamp":"2026-03-04T15:23:10Z","request":{"model":"redwood-llm-v1","prompt_len":312,"tokens":138},"client":{"sdk":"js", "sdk_version":"2.1.0","session_id":"s-123"}}'

- 2) Ingress & validation latency
  - Run 500 events at 5 rps from customer side during test window. Measure time-to-ack from ingress-gateway to telemetry-gatekeeper.
  - Acceptable: p95 < 200ms; if p95 between 200–400ms tag for follow-up optimization.

- 3) Rate-limit and quota checks
  - Confirm tenant quotas in telemetry-gatekeeper: default_quota limits and burst settings.
  - Example admin check (internal CLI):
    rwdctl telemetry quotas get --tenant acme-corp --env prod
    Expected sample output: "daily_quota: 5,000,000; burst_rate: 2000r/s; overage_action: throttle"

- 4) PII scrubbing and allowed fields
  - Confirm tenant-metrics-proxy scrubbing rules. Provide sample event with PII fields and verify removal.

- 5) Dashboard and SLI creation
  - Create tenant-level dashboard: latency_by_route, schema_failure_rate, event_ingest_rate, error_rate.
  - Define SLIs and target thresholds with customer: 
    - Event delivery success = 99.9% over 7d
    - Schema-failure-rate <= 0.5% (initial target)

Step-by-step onboarding procedure:
1. Preparation (CS + Eng alignment, 2–5 business days)
   a) CS collects prerequisites and creates an onboarding ticket in JIRA: ONB-<TENANT>-<YYYYMMDD>.
   b) Assign owners: CS lead, Observability Eng reviewer, Network Engineer for allowlist.
   c) Schedule 2-hour integration window and share IP allowlist and test key.

2. Dry-run validation (1–2 hours, non-production)
   a) Customer pushes 500 synthetic events.
   b) Run schema validation harness: 
      telemetry-harness run --target https://ingress-gateway.redwood.example --key <TEST_KEY> --events sample-set.json
   c) CS and Eng review harness report. If schema_failures >1%: iterate on mapping and retry.

3. Canary (low-volume production-like, 3–24 hours)
   a) Allow 1–5% of production traffic (or 10 rps, whichever is lower) routed to telemetry-gatekeeper.
   b) Monitor dashboards and alert noise for 24 hours.
   c) If alert noise increases >0.05% attributable to tenant, reduce canary volume and troubleshoot.

4. Full cutover (after canary and SLA signoff)
   a) CS issues a go/no-go and schedules final cutover with customer.
   b) Switch traffic and monitor p95 latency, success rate, schema failures at 1, 6, 24, 72 hour marks.

5. Handback and documentation (post-cutover, within 5 business days)
   a) Compile onboarding report and attach to JIRA ticket.
   b) Create tenant-specific dashboard folder and grant read access to customer stakeholders.
   c) Update runbook snippets and signal any config changes to infra as a change request.

Quick verification queries (Grafana/PromQL examples):
- Schema failure rate (last 24h):
  sum(rate(telemetry_schema_failures_total{tenant="acme-corp"}[24h])) / sum(rate(telemetry_events_received_total{tenant="acme-corp"}[24h]))

- Ingest latency p95 (last 1h):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(telemetry_ingest_latency_bucket{tenant="acme-corp"}[1h])) by (le))

Common failure modes and remediations:
- High schema_failure_rate (>1%)
  - Likely cause: SDK version mismatch or missing required fields.
  - Action: Ask customer to upgrade SDK or apply a mapping shim. Use telemetry-harness to generate failing samples and share stack traces.

- Sudden alert noise spike after cutover
  - Likely cause: low-cardinality fields or missing tenant scoping in metric labels.
  - Action: Re-scope metrics, add tenant label, and apply cardinality limits. Open change request to tenant-metrics-proxy.

- p95 ingest latency elevated
  - Likely cause: network peering or region mismatch.
  - Action: Check egress/ingress peering stats, validate region header, and consider routing via closer edge node.

Escalation matrix (when to page whom):
- Severity P0 (ingest down for tenant or >5% request failures for 15m):
  - Page: telemetry-oncall -> engage Observability Eng -> CS Lead -> Exec oncall if >60m.
- Severity P1 (schema failures >5% sustained for 30m or major alert noise increase):
  - Notify: eng-observability, cs-ops; Schedule 30-minute war room.
- Severity P2 (latency p95 >1s for 1 hour):
  - Triage with Network Eng and Observability Eng; schedule 2-hour fix window.

Rollback and safety net steps:
- Immediate rollback: update ingress routing to drop or re-route tenant traffic to a staging collector:
  rwdctl routing set --tenant acme-corp --target staging-collector --reason "emergency-rollback"
- Quarantine mode: enable quota throttle and scrubbers at telemetry-gatekeeper:
  rwdctl telemetry quarantine --tenant acme-corp --duration 30m --action throttle

Post-onboarding checklist (within 7 days):
- Confirm SLI/SLA targets in contract are instrumented and visible in QBR dashboards.
- Conduct a short post-mortem if any P1/P0 events occurred during onboarding.
- Move ticket to "Completed" and ensure knowledge transfer session recorded and stored in onboarding folder.

Operational guidance and best practices:
- Prefer SDK version parity: require customers to run a supported SDK (listed in SDK compatibility matrix).
- Low-cardinality labels only: advise customers to avoid user_id/session_id as primary metric labels; send as trace attribute instead.
- Use sampling for high-volume client events and send full traces for problematic sessions only.

Appendix A — Example minimal event schema (required fields):
{
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "event_type": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "request": { "model": "string", "tokens": "int" },
  "client": { "sdk": "string", "sdk_version": "string" }
}

Appendix B — Helpful CLI tools and contacts:
- telemetry-harness: repo internal at git@redwood:observability/telemetry-harness.git
- rwdctl (internal CLI) for telemetry and routing changes
- For compliance-sensitive telemetry (PII concerns), involve privacy@redwood.com before canary

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12: Created by Maya Chen
- 2026-02-10: Added canary acceptance thresholds and quarantine CLI commands (reviewer: Diego Alvarez)
- 2026-03-04: Updated SLI targets and added Grafana queries (reviewer: Priya Nambiar)

End of playbook.
